golden.sn: Lies on the vertical axis of symmetry

16459.en: If P = X_13, then A′B′C′ is the **5th Fermat-Dao equilateral triangle.** If P = X_14, then A′B′C′ is the **6th Fermat-Dao equilateral triangle.** See also X_16247 and X_16267.

ba.t: for the A-vertex of the 5th Fermat-Dao equilateral triangle:
for the A-vertex of the 6th Fermat-Dao equilateral triangle:

re: X_16459 = trilinear pole of the line X_6137X_11081
X_16459 = perspector of ABC and cross-triangle of ABC and circumcevian triangle of X_15
no: Let P be a point in the plane of a triangle ABC. Let Ba and Ca be points on BC such that the triangle PBaCa is equilateral. Define the pairs {Cb, Ab} and {Ab, Bc}cyclically. Let A′ be the point other than P that lies on the circles (PAcBc) and (PCbAb), and define B′ and C′ cyclically. If P = X_13 or P = X_14 then the triangle A′B′C′ is equilateral. (Dao Thanh Oai, March 7, 2018). The converse is true; i.e., if A′B′C′ is equilateral, then P = X_13 or P = X_14. (Dao Thanh Oai, March 14, 2018)

A′ = ((7 SA + 4 SW)*S^2 - 5 \(\sqrt{3}\) S (S^2 + SA^2) + 3 SA^3)/(- S + \(\sqrt{3}\) SA)^2 : * (\(\sqrt{3}\) (SA + SB) - 2 S)(SC + SA)/(- S + \(\sqrt{3}\) SB) : * (\(\sqrt{3}\) (SC + SA) - 2 S)(SA + SB)/(- S + \(\sqrt{3}\) SC). (These barycentrics and centers X_16461-X_16466 contributed by César Lozada, March 14, 2018)
